_meta.what_this_is: Several units (clinics, counties, stores -- whatever) each reporting how many of n trials were successes, all drawn from the SAME underlying success rate of 0.10. Because a small sample has high variance, the units with the most extreme observed RATES are the small ones -- both the highest and the lowest -- not because they are special but because small n is noisy. The honest signal is not the raw rate but how many standard errors it sits from the baseline: a modest rate over a huge sample can be a far stronger anomaly than an extreme rate over a tiny one.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The counts are hand-authored so the extreme raw rates (0.30 and 0.00) come from the smallest samples (n=20, n=25) and are within noise of the 0.10 baseline, while a large sample (n=5000) with an unremarkable 0.13 rate is by far the strongest signal. Every rate, standard error, and z-score is computed in smallnum.py.
